title: The Autopsy That Reached the Family — Left-Dominant Desmoplakin (DSP) Arrhythmogenic Cardiomyopathy Misread as Ischemic Scarring, Copy-Number MLPA Revisit & Cascade Family Screening

teenKit.tldr: A 37-year-old man's sudden death from a heart attack was originally blamed on common artery blockages, but a decade-long genetic investigation proved it was actually a rare, inherited heart muscle disease that threatened his living relatives.
teenKit.whyItMatters: This case proves that a single medical puzzle solved today can act as an invisible shield, protecting an entire family's future generations from hidden, inherited dangers.
keyTakeaways: An autopsy is not always the final answer; modern genetics and advanced lab tests can completely rewrite what we thought happened years later.
Left-Dominant Desmoplakin (DSP) Arrhythmogenic Cardiomyopathy is a sneaky genetic heart condition that gets easily mistaken for a standard heart attack caused by blocked arteries.
Cascade family screening means using one person's diagnosis to test living relatives, stopping genetic threats before they ever cause symptoms.

vocab.meaning: A thorough medical examination of a body after death to figure out exactly why and how the person died.
A disease of the heart muscle that makes it harder for the heart to pump blood effectively to the rest of the body.
Damage to heart tissue caused by a blocked blood supply, usually associated with a classic heart attack.
A systematic process of testing blood relatives for a newly discovered genetic disease to protect them early.

quiz.question: What was the initial, mistaken conclusion made after the 37-year-old man's sudden death in 2008?
options: A rare poison found in his water supply
A genetic disorder of the brain
Standard ischemic scarring from blocked arteries
A severe allergic reaction to a medication
quiz.explanation: The original autopsy misread the heart muscle damage as standard ischemic scarring, missing the true genetic culprit.

quiz.question: Why did investigators revisit the original case nearly a decade later?
options: To protect and screen the extended family members who were still alive
Because new laws required all old files to be reviewed
To find a missing piece of physical evidence from the basketball court
quiz.explanation: Revisiting the case allowed doctors to perform cascade screening to save living family members who might carry the same hidden gene.

quiz.question: What does 'Desmoplakin (DSP)' refer to in the context of this medical mystery?
options: A type of toxic chemical found in basketball courts
A brand of imaging machine used during autopsies
A specific gene associated with heart muscle structure that caused the hidden cardiomyopathy
A medication used to treat high blood pressure
quiz.explanation: DSP is a gene linked to cellular glue in the heart, and mutations in it can lead to dangerous, hidden arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.
